question.prompt:
Three triangles and a diamond balance nine dots. Also, one triangle balances a diamond and a dot. How many dots will balance two diamonds?

[Figure 1](figures/1990_AMC_8_Q24_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The second balance tells us that a triangle can be replaced by a diamond and a dot without changing the weight. Replace all three triangles in the first balance this way. Its left side then contains four diamonds and three dots, which together balance nine dots.

Remove three dots from each side. Four diamonds therefore balance \(9-3=6\) dots. Taking half of each side shows that two diamonds balance \(6\div2=3\) dots. The answer is \(\boxed{3}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Replace triangles with equal weights
